movers.name: Gen Digital
movers.headline: Earnings beat, raised guidance, no M&A fears
movers.what_happened: Gen Digital jumped nearly 16% after reporting fiscal Q2 results that topped analyst estimates on both revenue and earnings. The company also raised its full-year guidance for sales and EPS, and management clarified it is not pursuing a large acquisition, which eased investor concerns.
movers.why: The surge was driven by a strong earnings beat (EPS $0.74 vs $0.72 estimate, sales $1.369B vs $1.340B estimate), raised FY2027 guidance on both sales and EPS, and management's statement ruling out a 'transformative acquisition,' which removed uncertainty that had been weighing on the stock.

concept.name: Earnings beat and raise
concept.lesson: When a company not only beats quarterly estimates but also raises its forward guidance, the stock often jumps sharply because it signals improving fundamentals rather than a one-time surprise. Removing an overhang, like management denying a risky acquisition, can amplify the move by eliminating a specific fear investors had priced in.

prediction.reasoning: A genuine fundamental beat-and-raise plus removal of M&A uncertainty often leads to continued analyst upgrades and sustained buying interest over the following days, unlike moves driven by speculation or sentiment alone. However, after a 16% single-day pop some retracement or consolidation is possible, so confidence is only medium rather than high.

movers.name: Carvana
movers.headline: Record Q3 sales and raised guidance spark rally
movers.what_happened: Carvana jumped about 16% intraday and closed up 15.68% after reporting record third-quarter results, with the stock far outpacing a flat-to-down broader market. Shares had already moved higher in after-hours trading Wednesday night before extending gains through Thursday's session on heavy volume.
movers.why: Carvana posted record Q3 revenue of $8.04 billion (up 42% year-over-year) and record retail unit sales of 217,385 (up 39%), and management guided full-year adjusted EBITDA toward the high end of its range. Even though EPS missed analyst estimates, investors focused on the strength of unit growth, margin trajectory, and the raised EBITDA outlook, with Morgan Stanley naming it a top pick and several analysts reiterating Buy ratings despite trimming price targets.

concept.name: Earnings beat on growth, not EPS
concept.lesson: A stock can jump sharply even after missing EPS estimates if headline growth metrics (revenue, units sold) and forward guidance impress investors more than the bottom-line miss disappoints them. When analyzing earnings reactions, look beyond a single line item like EPS to see which metric the market is weighting most heavily that day.

prediction.reasoning: After a 15.68% single-day pop driven by a well-digested earnings beat, much of the good news is likely already priced in, and several analysts trimmed price targets even while staying bullish long-term, which can cap near-term upside. Large post-earnings gap-ups also sometimes see partial mean-reversion or profit-taking over the following days, but conviction here is low since the fundamental story (record growth, raised guidance) is genuinely strong and could keep attracting buyers.

movers.name: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings
movers.headline: Norwegian beats Q3, raises guidance on cost cuts
movers.what_happened: Norwegian Cruise Line jumped over 13% after reporting third-quarter results that beat Wall Street estimates on both earnings and revenue. The company raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance from $1.50 to $1.70, well above the $1.54 analysts expected, citing cost efficiency and stronger-than-expected close-in bookings.
movers.why: The move was driven by a beat-and-raise earnings report: Q3 GAAP EPS of $1.07 topped estimates by over 20%, and management lifted full-year guidance on the back of cost cuts and improved late-cycle demand, even though ticket revenue and 2027 bookings showed some softness.

concept.name: Earnings beat-and-raise
concept.lesson: When a company not only beats quarterly estimates but also raises its forward guidance, the stock often jumps sharply because investors revise their future profit expectations upward, not just react to the past quarter's results. The size of the move often depends on how low expectations were beforehand — a beaten-down stock like NCLH (down over 40% in 5 years) can snap back hard on good news.

prediction.reasoning: The strong beat-and-raise and positive 2027 commentary could sustain short-term momentum, but cautionary notes (falling ticket revenue, soft 2027 bookings, CFO transition) add uncertainty. Over 5 days, post-earnings drift could continue modestly in NCLH's favor versus SPY, but confidence is low given the stock's volatility and mixed underlying details.

movers.name: Huntington Ingalls Industries
movers.headline: Huge earnings beat, raised guidance send HII soaring
movers.what_happened: Huntington Ingalls jumped over 13% after reporting record third-quarter revenue and EPS that blew past Wall Street estimates. The company also raised its full-year shipbuilding revenue guidance and reported $32.4 billion in new contract awards, including a backlog that now covers roughly 90% of shipbuilding revenue through 2030.
movers.why: Q3 EPS of $5.48 beat the $4.42 estimate by nearly 24%, revenue of $3.54 billion topped expectations, and management raised FY26 sales and shipbuilding revenue guidance while highlighting record contract awards. This combination of a strong beat plus raised guidance and secured long-term backlog reassured investors about the defense contractor's growth trajectory.

concept.name: Earnings beat and raise
concept.lesson: When a company not only beats quarterly earnings and revenue estimates but also raises its forward guidance, the stock often reacts far more strongly than from the beat alone, because it signals improving fundamentals are expected to continue, not just a one-time surprise. Always check whether a big earnings-day move includes a guidance change, not just the historical numbers.

prediction.reasoning: A 13% single-day jump on a strong beat-and-raise with a long secured backlog (90% of shipbuilding revenue through 2030) suggests durable positive sentiment that often persists for several days as analysts upgrade price targets post-earnings. Some mean-reversion/profit-taking risk exists after such a large move, but the fundamental re-rating argument favors continued relative strength versus SPY over the next 5 trading days.

movers.name: Textron
movers.headline: Textron jumps on Q3 earnings beat, raised guidance
movers.what_happened: Textron shares surged about 12% after the company reported Q3 2026 earnings well above expectations and raised its full-year EPS and cash flow outlook. The stock gapped up at the open and held gains through the session while the broader S&P 500 slipped slightly.
movers.why: Textron posted non-GAAP EPS of $1.76, beating consensus of $1.43 by over 23%, driven by strong Textron Aviation deliveries and Textron Systems performance. The company raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $6.55-$6.65 (from $6.40-$6.60) and GAAP EPS guidance to $5.64-$5.74, both above analyst estimates, while also lifting its cash flow outlook.

concept.name: Earnings beat and raise
concept.lesson: When a company not only beats quarterly estimates but also raises its forward guidance above what analysts expected, the stock often jumps sharply because investors are repricing future earnings, not just celebrating the past quarter. The bigger the 'raise' relative to prior guidance and consensus, the bigger the typical reaction, since guidance shapes expectations for many quarters ahead.

prediction.reasoning: A strong beat-and-raise quarter with guidance now above consensus often leads to positive analyst estimate revisions and sustained buying interest in the days following the print, which could help TXT outperform SPY over the next 5 trading days. Confidence is medium because large single-day pops can also see some mean reversion or profit-taking, and the broader market/defense-aerospace sector sentiment could offset company-specific momentum.

movers.name: ServiceNow
movers.headline: ServiceNow crashes 27% on weak backlog guidance
movers.what_happened: ServiceNow reported Q3 earnings that beat revenue estimates but missed on adjusted EPS, and raised its full-year AI target. Despite the beat-and-raise, the stock cratered nearly 27%, its worst single-day drop in over 14 years, after guidance implied decelerating current remaining performance obligations (cRPO) growth into Q4.
movers.why: The sell-off was driven by ServiceNow guiding Q4 cRPO (a key backlog/bookings growth measure) to decelerate to around 18.5%, reigniting investor fears that AI disruption could be eroding software seat growth even as the company touts AI revenue gains. The miss on adjusted EPS added to the disappointment, and the news dragged down peers like Salesforce, Workday, SAP, and Fortinet (which also reported weak results the same day), signaling a broader re-rating of enterprise software stocks amid AI uncertainty.

concept.name: Guidance-driven selloff
concept.lesson: A company can beat on revenue and even raise some targets, yet still see its stock crash if a key forward-looking metric (like backlog or next-quarter guidance) disappoints. Markets price in expectations about the future, not just past results, so always check what a company says about what's coming next, not just what it already delivered.

prediction.reasoning: A 27% single-day drop reflects a serious re-rating of growth expectations, and historically such sharp guidance-driven selloffs in software names can see continued volatility or further downgrades in the following days as analysts revise models, even if some firms (like Piper Sandler) see long-term upside. Peer stocks (Salesforce, Workday, SAP) also fell, suggesting sector-wide pressure that could persist short-term. However, some analysts already flagged undervaluation, which could support a bounce, hence low confidence.

movers.name: Fortinet
movers.headline: Fortinet plunges 20% despite earnings beat
movers.what_happened: Fortinet reported Q3 revenue, billings and earnings that beat estimates and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance, yet the stock cratered over 20%, its worst day in years. The sell-off dragged down peers like Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike and Zscaler as well as other software names like ServiceNow and F5.
movers.why: Investors focused on a cut to the full-year services revenue forecast and signs of slowing product growth (37% vs prior quarters), which analysts like BofA flagged as a 'disappointing slowdown' that overshadowed the headline beat-and-raise. After a stock up over 100% YTD, the market punished any sign of decelerating growth, especially after F5 saw a similar 20% drop a day earlier on soft guidance, suggesting a broader shift where Wall Street is no longer rewarding AI/software beats unless forward metrics are flawless.

concept.name: Buy the rumor, sell the news
concept.lesson: When a stock has rallied hard (FTNT was up over 100% YTD), expectations get priced in so high that even a genuine beat-and-raise quarter isn't enough — the market instead zeroes in on any soft spot in the details (here, a services revenue forecast cut and slowing product growth) and sells hard. Always check what the market had already priced in before assuming 'good numbers' will move a stock up.

prediction.reasoning: A 20%+ single-day drop on a guidance nuance often triggers a few days of continued uncertainty and analyst downgrades as the Street digests the services slowdown, and sector-wide skepticism toward software/AI names (seen also in ServiceNow, F5) could keep pressure on FTNT. However, the stock could also stabilize or bounce after such a sharp overreaction since fundamentals (raised full-year guidance) were still positive, so confidence is low.

movers.name: Marvell Technology
movers.headline: Marvell plunges on reported $83B Lumentum takeover talks
movers.what_happened: Marvell Technology shares dropped about 13% after Bloomberg reported it was in advanced talks to acquire optical components maker Lumentum Holdings. The decline came alongside a broader tech selloff triggered by Alphabet's earnings miss, but Marvell's drop was far steeper than the market or its chip peers.
movers.why: Investors reacted negatively to reports that Marvell is near a deal to buy Lumentum, an optics supplier worth roughly a third of Marvell's market cap, likely financed with a large amount of new Marvell stock. The market worried about dilution, deal price, and integration risk even though the acquisition would bolster Marvell's AI data center optics capabilities.

concept.name: Acquirer sell-off
concept.lesson: When a company announces or is reported to be pursuing a large acquisition, its stock often falls even if the deal is strategically sound. Investors worry about overpaying, taking on debt, issuing dilutive new shares, and the risk that integration won't go smoothly. Meanwhile the target company's stock usually rises toward the expected buyout price. This pattern repeats across many M&A situations, so a stock dropping on 'we're buying X' news is a classic, predictable reaction worth recognizing rather than panicking over.

prediction.reasoning: The stock fell sharply on deal uncertainty and dilution fears, and these concerns (financing structure, premium paid, regulatory review) are unlikely to be resolved within 5 trading days, which could keep pressure on shares or produce continued volatility as more details emerge. However, a denial, a renegotiated/smaller deal, or a market-wide tech rebound could reverse much of the move quickly, so confidence is low.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
movers.headline: Alphabet's worst day ever on AI spending fears
movers.what_happened: Alphabet shares plunged over 12%, their largest single-day drop on record, wiping out nearly $500 billion in market value. The sell-off came despite 25% revenue growth and dragged down the broader Nasdaq and S&P 500.
movers.why: Alphabet reported Q3 earnings showing slowing Search advertising growth, negative free cash flow for a second straight quarter, and soaring AI-related capital spending. Investors reacted negatively to the combination of a profit miss and ballooning AI infrastructure costs even though Google Cloud revenue more than doubled, fearing the AI spending spree isn't yet paying off.

concept.name: Earnings reaction vs. headline growth
concept.lesson: A company can post strong top-line growth (here, 25% revenue growth) and still see its stock crash if investors focus on other signals, like deteriorating cash flow or spending that outpaces returns. Markets price in expectations, not just absolute numbers, so always check what estimates and cash flow trends looked like, not just whether revenue grew.

prediction.reasoning: A 12%+ drop of this magnitude often triggers continued uncertainty and volatility as analysts digest AI capex and cash flow concerns, and the negative sentiment spilled into other mega-cap tech (Amazon, chips) the same week, suggesting a sector-wide re-rating rather than an isolated event. However, some analysts (SeekingAlpha bulls) argue the sell-off is overdone given strong Cloud growth, so a bounce-back is possible, keeping confidence low.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class C)
movers.headline: Alphabet crashes record 12% on AI spending fears
movers.what_happened: Alphabet shares fell more than 12%, their worst single-day drop on record, erasing roughly $500 billion in market value. The decline came despite the company reporting 25% revenue growth and a doubling of Google Cloud revenue in its third-quarter results.
movers.why: Investors were spooked by Alphabet's massive AI capital spending, which pushed free cash flow negative for a second straight quarter, and by slowing Search advertising growth amid rising competition. Even strong cloud growth and overall revenue beats couldn't offset concerns that AI infrastructure costs are outpacing returns, and the selloff dragged down other tech stocks like Amazon that reported AI-heavy results the same week.

concept.name: Earnings reaction vs. fundamentals
concept.lesson: A stock can drop sharply even after reporting strong headline growth if investors focus on a specific worry—here, negative free cash flow from AI spending and slowing ad growth. Markets price in expectations, not just absolute results, so the reaction to earnings depends on which numbers investors decide matter most that day.

prediction.reasoning: A record one-day drop of this magnitude often sees continued volatility and cautious sentiment in the days following as analysts digest the cash flow concerns and the market reassesses AI capex across the sector (Amazon also fell on similar worries). However, several analysts (SeekingAlpha pieces) argue the selloff is overdone given strong cloud growth, which could support a bounce. Given the mixed signals, this is a low-confidence call that GOOG underperforms SPY over the next 5 trading days as the market continues to digest AI spending concerns.
